# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 1
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 1

---

1. He was sitting on the Mount of Olives when we — his disciples — gathered around him one by one, pleading with him: "Tell us — what will the signs be? What will we see when you return, when the world comes to its end?"

2. Our Lord looked at us and said: "Be careful. Don't let anyone lead you astray. Many will show up claiming my name, declaring, 'I am the Christ.' Don't believe them. Don't even approach them.

3. Deceivers will come — false prophets who will construct elaborate teachings and conflicting doctrines, all designed to trap those who are already on the road to ruin.

4. They are children of destruction. But then — after all of this — my Father will come. God himself will come to raise the dead, to stand in judgment over the living and the dead alike, and to give each person exactly what their deeds have earned."

5. As he spoke he held out his right hand, and there in his palm we saw the souls of all humanity — and an image of everything that would unfold on that final day.

6. I watched as the wicked were handed over to the angels of punishment, who herded them toward the outer darkness.

7. Then he said: "When the fig tree puts forth its first shoots — that is when it will happen. In those final days, deceivers and false prophets will rise up and promote clashing doctrines to trap the perishing.

8. Here is what the parable of the fig tree means: once its shoots appear and its branches spread, the end of the age is at the door."

9. I said to him: "Lord, explain the fig tree parable more fully. Help us understand it."

10. He answered: "The fig tree is the house of Israel — don't you see it? Think of a man who plants a fig tree in his garden. Year after year it bears no fruit. Finally he says to the gardener: 'Dig this tree up. It is wasting the soil.'

11. But the gardener says: 'Give it one more chance. Let me work the soil around it and water it; if it still won't bear fruit, we'll tear it out by the roots and put something else in its place.'

12. The fig tree is the house of Israel. I tell you the truth: when its branches shoot forth in the last days, false Christs will arrive full of false promises, declaring, 'I am the Christ — I have come at last.'

13. And when people see what these false Christs truly are, many will still follow them, abandoning the one our fathers honored — the true Christ, the one they crucified, committing their great sin.

14. But that deceiver is not the Christ. And when they finally reject him, he will turn to the sword, and many will die for their faith."

15. Those will be the days when the fig tree — Israel — bursts into bloom. Many will fall by the deceiver's hand. They will be martyrs.

16. "Enoch and Elijah will be sent to warn them: this is the Deceiver. He will come to the world armed with signs and wonders, all of them lies.

17. And those who die at his hand — they will not have died in vain. They will be counted among the faithful martyrs, the righteous ones who gave God pleasure throughout their lives."

---
*PNEUMA renders for impact and clarity, prioritizing the apocalyptic urgency of the discourse. The fig-tree allegory is made transparent without losing its symbolic weight.*
